title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 154 (Allotment of Director Identification Number)

content.overview: Section 154 provides that the Central Government shall, within the prescribed period from receipt of an application under section 153, allot a Director Identification Number to the applicant in such manner as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Central Government allots a DIN within the prescribed period after a valid application under s. 153; allotment is administrative and enables appointment under s. 152.
content.study: The Central Government shall, within such time as may be prescribed, allot a Director Identification Number to an applicant under section 153 in such manner as may be prescribed. Allotment is an administrative act following a complete application. The DIN is quoted on consents, returns and filings. A wrong or duplicate allotment is addressed under the correction and prohibition provisions (ss. 155–156 and related rules), not by treating the person as having two valid DINs. Current-law framing: confirm application under s. 153; identify allotment by the Central Government within the prescribed period; link to appointment under s. 152.

sections.heading: Who Allots
sections.body: The Central Government allots the Director Identification Number.

sections.heading: Trigger and Time
sections.body: Allotment follows an application under section 153 and must be made within the prescribed period.

sections.heading: Manner
sections.body: Allotment is in such manner as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Once allotted, the DIN is the unique identifier used for appointment, consent and ROC filings under the connected sections.

examples.title: Timely allotment
examples.body: An individual applies under s. 153. The Central Government allots a DIN within the prescribed period. The person may then consent to appointment under s. 152.

examples.title: No application, no allotment
examples.body: Without a complete application under s. 153, there is nothing for the Central Government to allot under s. 154.

hypotheticals.question: Does allotment of a DIN itself appoint the person as a director?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 154 is allotment only. Appointment remains under section 152 (and composition under s. 149).

distinctions.title: Allotment of DIN (s. 154) vs application for DIN (s. 153)
distinctions.left: Central Government’s duty to allot within prescribed time
distinctions.right: Individual’s duty to apply in prescribed form with fee

misconceptions.trap: DIN allotment is the same as appointment as director.
misconceptions.correction: Allotment under s. 154 is only the grant of the identifier; appointment is a separate act under s. 152.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 154 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm application under s. 153. II. State Central Government allotment within prescribed period. III. Link to appointment under s. 152. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Application facts; allotment status; timeline; precise relief.

examTips: Allotment is by the Central Government.
Does not itself appoint the director.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Unique director identification is completed by governmental allotment following a statutory application.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 154 is the allotment leg of the DIN regime.
